extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of philosophy and psychology (esp. readers of William James and Bergson)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing philosophical/psychological exposition that balances conceptual analysis and immediate, sympathetic acquaintance with lived experience. Emphasizes methods for describing motion, time, causation, and inner life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perception as discrete pulses ('drops') / felt times come in drops
rubrics_metrics.description: All sensible experiences, as we get them immediately, change by discrete pulses of perception; 'time itself comes in drops.' Fechner's 'threshold' names the quantitative discreteness in perceived change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When describing perception or temporality, treat immediate experience as composed of discrete felt increments rather than assuming a homogeneous continuous time; use examples (e.g., a lump of sugar melting) to show that felt durations coexist and overlap and resist a single objective measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptual decomposition is retrospective / post-mortem
rubrics_metrics.description: Concepts are 'flowers gathered' or 'snap-shots'—retrospective cuts out of the stream of time made for practical/intellectual use; they are samples, not the living process itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that conceptual analysis arrests movement and cannot by itself explain how phenomena 'get made.' Use concepts as tools for calculation or communication but not as substitutes for an account of the inner, productive processes of reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellect's function is primarily practical rather than speculative
rubrics_metrics.description: The intellect's original and surviving role is to guide practical adaptation (to make short cuts through experience); theoretical knowledge (about things) differs from the deeper speculative or sympathetic knowledge of inner life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing, distinguish between synoptic, calculable knowledge (useful for manipulation and prediction) and the kind of intimate, sympathetic understanding that gives insight into inner activities; choose form and method according to which one you aim to deliver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reducing motion to static conceptual positions
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical/conceptual definitions (e.g., motion as 'occupancy of serially successive points of space at serially successive instants of time') capture positions but omit how a body gets from one to another; such static cuts make movement unintelligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To convey movement or flux, foreground lived impetus and continuity rather than sequences of discretized states; illustrate the lived onrush (e.g., Achilles' experienced impetus) instead of only the abstract positions or instants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprehend inner nature via direct experience or sympathetic imagination
rubrics_metrics.description: The thickness of reality can be grasped either by being a part of reality oneself or by evoking it in imagination through sympathetic divination of another's inner life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In prose aiming to reveal inner life, use immersive, sympathetic description and imaginative empathy rather than relying solely on abstract conceptual exposition; 'place yourself at the centre' of the thing to disclose its movements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose method appropriate to subject matter (conceptual for space/matter; sympathetic for moral/psychic facts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conceptual methods succeed best in sciences of space and matter where external transformations are handled; moral or psychic facts require experiential/sympathetic methods rather than mechanical metaphors or atomizing abstractions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match form and method to domain: employ precise conceptual schemata for spatial/physical description and adopt evocative, sympathetic, phenomenological techniques for moral/psychological topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware that a concept is a 'that-and-no-other' (exclusive cut)
rubrics_metrics.description: When we conceptualize we 'cut out and fix' and exclude everything but what we have fixed; conceptually 'time excludes space,' 'motion and rest exclude each other,' etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid letting conceptual categories falsely imply mutual exclusivity in contexts where aspects co-penetrate; in creative or philosophical description, show overlapping qualities and resist treating attributes as mutually exclusive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portray compenetration of sameness and difference in experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Concrete experience is an endosmosis of same and different — experiences com-penetrate so that aspects (quality, duration, extension, intensity, clearness) coexist and cannot be isolated cleanly as concepts demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In description, represent how multiple aspects are simultaneously present and interwoven (e.g., two skin spots that each match a third yet feel different); use examples of sensory conflation to demonstrate this telescoping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depict continuity as partial decay and partial growth with a persistent nucleus
rubrics_metrics.description: Change is not annihilation followed by creation but gradual partial decay and growth with a nucleus of relative constancy that takes on and drops off elements over time (log-carrying analogy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When depicting transformation, show the ongoing continuity—a persisting centre that acquires and loses parts—rather than abrupt, absolute replacements; render intermediate, overlapping stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Represent causation and dynamic influence between finite things as real
rubrics_metrics.description: Intellectualism's conceptual logic tends to deny that finite things can act on one another; lived experience shows dynamic currents and influences passing between selves and bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portray interaction as genuine transfer or mutual impact (thoughts animating bodies, persons influencing each other) rather than as isolated, self-contained conceptual units; dramatize the mechanisms or felt effects of influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use concepts for synoptic mapping but not as substitutes for insight
rubrics_metrics.description: Concepts allow broad, calculable, synoptic treatment (plotting, interpolating, prediction) but they do not penetrate the 'inner dimension' occupied by activities that make reality go.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your aim is overview or prediction, employ conceptual schemata; if your aim is insight into process or motive, use immersion, narrative, and sympathetic rendering to reach the interior life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer sensation and flux over immutable universals to reveal reality
rubrics_metrics.description: Bergson inverts Platonic doctrine: instead of thinking intellectual knowledge deeper, Bergson calls it superficial and urges a turn to sensation and the lived flux to 'know' reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In philosophical or literary work that seeks to disclose reality's nature, foreground sensory immediacy and dynamic flux; avoid over-reliance on abstract, static universals that sterilize living processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Install yourself inside the phenomenon before abstracting
rubrics_metrics.description: If one 'places oneself d'emblée inside of the living, moving, active thickness of the real,' then intellectual substitutions and abstractions follow intelligibly; without that interior standpoint, conceptual reconstructions cannot reconstitute wholeness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When creating concepts, first strive for an intuitive, sympathetic immersion in the subject; produce abstractions only after living the phenomenon inwardly so the abstractions reflect its inner movement rather than merely amputating it.
